native_result.query: What is the average length of original papers in Experimental Economics and that in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: Studies in Experimental Economics tend to have longer original papers compared to Psychology. The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28 pages, whereas in Psychology, the average is 11 pages.
native_result.HypoB: In the sample of original papers underlying these replication projects — table 1 study_data (927 rows / 141 unique O/R pairs), where original-paper length is the field `length` (pages of the original paper) and the two categories are defined solely by `project` (`ee` = Experimental Economics, n=18, exactly matching discipline=='Economics'; `rpp` = Psychology, n=97; `journal` not used for screening) — Experimental Economics original papers average 28.0 pages, whereas Psychology (rpp) original papers average 11.22 pages, a difference of 16.78 pages or about 2.5x (bootstrap 95% CI for the difference 13.3-20.4 pages; for the ratio 2.12-2.95; Welch t=9.06, p=7.4e-09; Mann-Whitney U=1681.5, p=4.5e-10). Medians are 27.5 vs 9.0 pages (SD 7.37 vs 6.30; IQR 23.5-30.0 vs 7-16; range 16-45 vs 1-31, right-skewed on the psychology side). We hypothesise that this gap is at least partly a product of field/journal length conventions rather than of research scale or quality: all 18 ee papers are AER/QJE articles whose page counts include figures, tables and appendices, while the rpp originals are Psychological Science / JPSP / JEPLMC articles that include 2-3 page short reports. This characterises the papers in this replication sample only and is not a general claim about Experimental Economics versus Psychology as fields.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Profiled both tables; confirmed table2 (143x15) has no length field, so it was used only to cross-check that its 18 'Experimental Economics' studies correspond to the 18 ee rows. 2) Verified row/id structure: 927 rows = 141 unique ids; ee 18 rows=18 ids and rpp 97 rows=97 ids; asserted 0 duplicate ids and 0 missing `length` in the ee+rpp subset (115 rows); confirmed `length` is constant within all 141 ids. 3) Filtered project in {ee, rpp} (no discipline/journal filtering; confirmed ee disciplines == {Economics}); kept drop==True rows, same-title multiple target effects and very short records per the approved spec. 4) Computed per-group n, mean, median, SD, IQR, min/max and skewness; bootstrap 95% CIs (20000 resamples, seed 20261023) for both means, the difference and the ratio; Welch t-test and Mann-Whitney U plus Cohen's d and rank-biserial. 5) Built an 8-row sensitivity table (main; exclude drop==True; dedup by title; exclude length<=3; exclude only length==1; ee restricted to AER; Psychology widened to rpp+ml1+ml3 at row level and at paper level). 6) Produced a data-quality report (id/row relations, flag distributions, rpp id gaps 97 of 1-167, extreme-value inventory and their pull on the mean). Executed with python3/pandas 3.0.2/scipy 1.16.0; full console output preserved in run_main.log and results_summary.txt.
